knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 1.1.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly contrasts data source types and one large-set characteristic that affects analysis?
knowledge_checks.body: Select source characteristics and scale constraint.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Quality and bias depend on source design, not size alone. Large scale can add engineering constraints rather than remove them.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Source quality varies; large volume does not auto-imply fitness.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Bigger-is-better, deferred trust checks, or ignoring scale limits.

choices.label: Sources differ in origin and quality (for example administrative records versus voluntary surveys bring different bias and coverage risks). Extremely large sets add scale constraints such as storage, compute limits, or need for sampling despite volume.
A larger file is automatically better data because volume implies representativeness and removes selection concerns.
Source characteristics matter only after modelling is complete; during exploration all files may be treated as equally trustworthy.
Extremely large data sets always remove the need for sampling or distributed tooling because every row can always be processed locally without constraint.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 1.1.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Compare an administrative claims extract with a voluntary customer survey, both used for the same pricing question. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Name trust characteristics and a large-set constraint; refuse bigger-is-better.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Bias and coverage differ by source mechanism. Row count does not replace representativeness or remove scale work.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Compare bias/coverage; large n does not imply better data.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Row-count superiority, deferred trust, or volume cures bias.

choices.label: Examples: selection or response bias (survey versus administrative coverage), completeness or granularity of fields, measurement error. Large scale may still require sampling or distributed tooling and does not fix representativeness by itself. Volume alone is not automatically better data.
The administrative extract is always superior because it has more rows, so source characteristics need not be compared.
Both sources are equally trustworthy during EDA because trust is assessed only after the final model is chosen.
Extremely large survey files remove bias automatically because every respondent row is included in the analysis file.

worked_example.title: Contrast admin claims extract with a voluntary survey
worked_example.problem_statement: The same pricing question can be answered from an administrative claims extract or from a voluntary customer survey. Contrast the two sources on bias or coverage, and state why a very large survey sample size does not automatically make the survey the better source.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Compare selection/coverage risks first, then separate volume from representativeness.

steps.label: Contrast bias and coverage
steps.attempt_cue: Name one bias or coverage difference between admin extract and survey.
steps.explanation: Administrative records cover booked claims but may miss unreported events or soft fields. Voluntary surveys often suffer response or selection bias and uneven coverage of the risk population.
steps.calculation: Contrast: admin coverage vs survey response/selection bias (and field completeness)
steps.result: Sources differ in bias and coverage risks

steps.label: Note large-set constraints without equating volume to quality
steps.attempt_cue: State one scale issue and refuse 'larger n ⇒ better data'.
steps.explanation: Extremely large sets can still need sampling or distributed tooling. Large n does not repair non-representativeness by itself.
steps.calculation: Large n ≠ automatic fitness; scale may still require sampling/tooling
steps.result: Volume is not automatically better data

steps.label: Judgment for the pricing question
steps.attempt_cue: State how to choose between A and B for pricing.
steps.explanation: Choose by matching source bias, coverage, and measurement properties to the pricing question, not by raw row count alone.
steps.calculation: Decision rule: fitness = bias/coverage/measurement match, not n-max
steps.result: Prefer source fitness over largest n

worked_example.final_answer: Admin extract and voluntary survey differ in selection/response bias and coverage. Large survey n does not automatically fix representativeness or make the survey better for the pricing question.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Assuming the voluntary survey is better whenever its row count exceeds the admin extract, without comparing bias, coverage, and measurement quality for the pricing use.
